title: Backspace String Compare
spaceBreakdown:
- int i, j, skipS, skipT: 4 scalar integers → O(1)
- No containers, no recursion, no heap allocation
- Not counted: input strings s and t
approach: Process both strings right-to-left with two pointers. Maintain a backspace counter per string: on '#', increment the counter and move left; on a regular character with pending backspaces, decrement the counter and move left; otherwise the character is a "survivor" ready to compare. Compare survivors from both strings one at a time - if they ever differ, or one string has a survivor while the other is exhausted, return false.
hints: If you read each string from the last character backward, what can you determine about each character before you decide to compare it? A '#' erases the character typed immediately before it, so 'ab#c' becomes 'ac'.

Use two pointers, one per string, both starting at the last index and moving left. For s = "ab#c", start at index 3 ('c'): it is not '#' and no backspaces are pending, so it is a character to compare.

```
i = len(s)-1, j = len(t)-1, skipS = 0, skipT = 0
while i >= 0 or j >= 0:
    move i left past '#' (incrementing skipS) and past deleted chars (decrementing skipS)
    move j left past '#' (incrementing skipT) and past deleted chars (decrementing skipT)
    if both valid: compare s[i] vs t[j], then i--, j--
    if only one valid: return false
return true
```

**One string exhausts first** - one string has more surviving characters than the other
`s = "a", t = "ba"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: using `while (i >= 0 && j >= 0)` instead of `||` in the outer loop → exits when i = -1, j = 0, returns true

**Consecutive backspaces** - multiple '#' in a row each erase a separate character
`s = "ab##", t = "c#d#"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: setting `skipS = 1` on each '#' instead of `skipS++` → s keeps 'a', returns false

**Leading backspace** - '#' at index 0 with nothing before it to erase
`s = "#a", t = "a"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: running `while (skipS > 0) { skipS--; i--; }` without checking `i >= 0` → i goes negative, accesses s[-1]

**Single character mismatch** - minimal input where the two strings differ
`s = "a", t = "b"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: using `while (i > 0 || j > 0)` instead of `>= 0` → never processes index 0, returns true

followUps.q: Can you solve it in O(n) time and O(1) space?
followUps.a: Yes - the two-pointer right-to-left approach above already achieves this. By scanning backward, you know exactly how many backspaces are pending before you commit to comparing a character, so no result string is ever built.

followUps.q: What if '#' deletes the last k characters instead of just one?
followUps.a: Replace `skipS++` with `skipS += k` (and likewise for skipT) when you encounter '#'. The rest of the logic is identical - each backspace now skips k characters. Time remains O(n + m), space O(1).

followUps.q: What if the strings arrive as a one-pass left-to-right stream with no random access?
followUps.a: Maintain a write pointer into a per-string buffer; on '#', decrement the pointer (clamped at 0); on a regular character, write it and increment. Compare the two buffers at the end. This uses O(n) space in the worst case (no backspaces), so the right-to-left two-pointer method is strictly better when random access is available.
